factory_version.description: Factory version this product was set up with.

models.description: Model per role, passed to the CLI as is. Unset roles use the CLI default.

check.description: Lint, build and test commands. Run by the runner before any model review.

workflow.description: The workflow items run unless they name their own; feature when unset. The product's .factory/workflows/<name>.yaml replaces the factory's.

paths.description: Named path lists that a workflow step's `when.touches` can use, for example ui: ["src/ui/**"] to bring in the UX designer's review.

specialists.description: Specialist reviewers this product turns on, for example [security-reviewer] for a product that holds keys or money, or [ux-designer] with paths.ui set. The team proposes them; the owner decides.

deploy.description: Commands per environment for `asf deploy <env>`, for example production: ["./deploy.sh production"]. The runner runs them, outside the sandbox and with your own environment and credentials, only when you run asf deploy; agents never do.

tracker.description: Where tickets and the conversation with the owner live. Unset: the backlog/ folder is the tracker.

project.description: Jira project key, for example AI.

owner.description: The owner's Atlassian account id. Only tickets they reported and comments they wrote count; everything else is untrusted data.

intake_status.description: Tickets in this status become new backlog items.

intake_filter.description: More JQL a ticket must match to be taken in, for a project several products share, for example: labels = cardano-wallet AND issuetype != Epic. The owner-only rule still applies.

digest.description: A ticket the owner made for the product as a whole. The factory posts a digest of each day there, and the board whenever the owner comments "/status".

statuses.description: Statuses the factory moves tickets to, to show where they are. Unset ones are left alone.

integration_branch.description: When set, items branch from it and those that pass checks and review merge into it on their own; the owner releases it into base_branch in batches with `asf release`. Items that touch owner_paths, or that the tech lead escalates, still wait for the owner one by one.
